## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-7-2-trajectory-analysis-using-slingshot/>

Part 3 of 3. The Slingshot result from part 2 is checked against biology and
used: known marker genes are correlated with pseudotime (naive markers such as
CCR7, LEF1 and TCF7 should decrease; effector markers such as GZMB, PRF1 and
NKG7 should increase), pseudotime is compared between conditions, genes
correlated with pseudotime are identified, and pseudotime, lineage and lineage
weights are added back to the Seurat object.

The gene-wise Spearman correlation loop runs one `cor.test()` per gene over
all genes in the object and is slow.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 11-14). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load required libraries
#-----------------------------------------------

# Core trajectory analysis
library(slingshot)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(princurve)
library(TrajectoryUtils)

# Single-cell analysis infrastructure
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)

# Data manipulation
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Visualization
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)
library(scales)
library(grDevices)

source(here::here("helper_functions", "params_read.R"))
params <- params_ingest()

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
traj.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$traj.subdir)

# Create organized output directories
for (d in c("plots/pseudotime", "results")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(traj.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(traj.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

# Condition levels and colors from params
condition.colors <- setNames(unlist(params$condition.palette), unlist(params$condition.levels))
```

## Biological validation: marker genes

If the trajectory direction is biologically sensible, naive T cell markers
(CCR7, LEF1, TCF7) should be negatively correlated with pseudotime and
cytotoxic/effector markers (GZMB, PRF1, NKG7) positively correlated. The
direction is set by the start cluster chosen in part 2; with an automatically
chosen start, check this before interpreting the trajectory.

```{r step3_markers}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 11: Validate T/NK trajectory with marker genes
#-----------------------------------------------

# Test known T cell markers
marker_genes <- unlist(params$marker.genes)
available_markers <- marker_genes[marker_genes %in% rownames(sce)]

if (length(available_markers) > 0) {
  cat("Testing known markers along pseudotime...\n\n")

  for (gene in available_markers) {
    expr <- logcounts(sce)[gene, ]
    # NOTE: `use` is not an argument of cor.test() and is ignored (cor.test
    # already drops incomplete pairs)
    cor_test <- cor.test(sce$slingshot_pseudotime, expr,
                         method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")

    cat(sprintf("%s: correlation = %.3f, p-value = %.2e\n",
                gene, cor_test$estimate, cor_test$p.value))
  }
}
```

## Treatment effects on the T/NK trajectory

```{r step4_condition, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 12: Test treatment effects on T/NK pseudotime
#-----------------------------------------------

# Statistical test
wilcox_test <- wilcox.test(pseudotime ~ condition, data = umap_df)

cat("Wilcoxon rank-sum test:\n")
cat("  W statistic:", wilcox_test$statistic, "\n")
cat("  P-value:", format(wilcox_test$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n\n")

# Median by condition
median_summary <- umap_df %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    median_pt = median(pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_pt = mean(pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cat("Pseudotime by condition:\n")
print(as.data.frame(median_summary))

# Density plot
p_density <- ggplot(umap_df, aes(x = pseudotime, fill = condition)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = condition.colors) +
  labs(title = "T/NK Pseudotime Distribution by Condition",
       x = "Pseudotime", y = "Density") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
print(p_density)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/pseudotime/05_pseudotime_by_condition_T_NK.png"),
       p_density, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Identify trajectory-associated genes

Genes are ranked by Spearman correlation between log-normalized expression and
the consensus pseudotime, using only the T/NK cells.

```{r step5_trajectory_genes}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 13: Identify pseudotime-dependent genes in T/NK lineage
#-----------------------------------------------

# Use T/NK SCE object (not all cell types!)
expr_mat <- logcounts(sce)
pt <- sce$slingshot_pseudotime

cat("Testing", nrow(expr_mat), "genes across", ncol(sce), "T/NK cells\n\n")

# Test correlations
gene_results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(expr_mat)), function(i) {
  if (i %% 1000 == 0) cat("  Tested", i, "genes...\n")

  gene_expr <- expr_mat[i, ]

  if (sum(gene_expr > 0) < params$gene.min_cells) {
    return(data.frame(gene = rownames(expr_mat)[i], correlation = NA, p_value = NA))
  }

  cor_test <- cor.test(pt, gene_expr, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

  data.frame(
    gene = rownames(expr_mat)[i],
    correlation = as.numeric(cor_test$estimate),
    p_value = cor_test$p.value
  )
})

gene_results_df <- do.call(rbind, gene_results)
gene_results_df <- gene_results_df[!is.na(gene_results_df$p_value), ]
gene_results_df$q_value <- p.adjust(gene_results_df$p_value, method = "fdr")
gene_results_df <- gene_results_df[order(abs(gene_results_df$correlation), decreasing = TRUE), ]

sig_genes <- gene_results_df[gene_results_df$q_value < params$gene.q, ]

cat("Significant genes (q <", params$gene.q, "):", nrow(sig_genes), "\n")
cat("Positively correlated (increase along trajectory):", sum(sig_genes$correlation > 0), "\n")
cat("Negatively correlated (decrease along trajectory):", sum(sig_genes$correlation < 0), "\n\n")

cat("Top", params$genes.top_n, "genes:\n")
print(head(sig_genes, params$genes.top_n))

write.csv(sig_genes, file.path(traj.dir, "results/slingshot_T_NK_pseudotime_genes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Integrate T/NK results back into Seurat

```{r step6_to_seurat, fig.width = 16, fig.height = 6}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 14: Transfer T/NK trajectory results to Seurat
#-----------------------------------------------

# Create Seurat object for T/NK cells with trajectory info
seurat_t_nk$slingshot_pseudotime <- sce$slingshot_pseudotime
seurat_t_nk$slingshot_lineage <- sce$primary_lineage

# Add lineage weights
for (i in 1:ncol(curve_weights)) {
  seurat_t_nk@meta.data[[paste0("lineage_", i, "_weight")]] <- curve_weights[, i]
}

# Visualize in Seurat
p_seurat_pseudotime <- FeaturePlot(
  seurat_t_nk,
  features = "slingshot_pseudotime",
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  pt.size = 1
) +
  scale_color_viridis(option = "plasma") +
  ggtitle("T/NK Slingshot Pseudotime (Seurat)")

p_seurat_lineage <- DimPlot(
  seurat_t_nk,
  group.by = "slingshot_lineage",
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  pt.size = 1
) +
  ggtitle("T/NK Lineage Assignment (Seurat)")

p_combined <- p_seurat_pseudotime | p_seurat_lineage
print(p_combined)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/pseudotime/06_slingshot_T_NK_in_seurat.png"),
       p_combined, width = 16, height = 6, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Save T/NK object with trajectory
saveRDS(seurat_t_nk, file.path(traj.dir, "results/seurat_T_NK_with_slingshot.rds"))
```
